A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CellFluxRL and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Existing material can be matched reliably; v4 adds Appendix F and Table 5.

before.justification: v1 reports original BBBC021 experiments comparing CellFluxRL with generative baselines, plus test-time scaling, sensitivity analyses, reward ablations, and appendix results.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and adds evaluation using independently trained classifiers and an alternative segmentation pipeline in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The CellFlux base model, seven training rewards, DiffusionNFT optimization, and best-of-N inference remain unchanged. The additional classifiers and segmentation pipeline are used only for evaluation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same BBBC021 cellular perturbation task. The held-out evaluation concerns reward implementations, without adding datasets, populations, perturbation scenarios, or input conditions.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains PhenDiff, IMPA, and CellFlux as baselines. New Table 5 compares CellFluxRL with the existing CellFlux baseline; CLIP, DINOv2, and StarDist serve as evaluators, not additional competing generation methods.

E3.justification: Appendix F adds a protocol evaluating MoA with held-out CLIP and DINOv2 classifiers and nucleus containment with StarDist. Existing data splits, generation training settings, and test-time scaling procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix F adds a substantive reward-hacking robustness study: functional and structural improvements are tested using three evaluator implementations excluded from RL training. This directly examines evaluator dependence, which v1's KL sensitivity, reward ablations, and qualitative cases did not test.

E5.justification: No repeated-run counts, seed information, uncertainty estimation, or significance testing are added or revised. Table 5 continues reporting point estimates without uncertainty intervals.

E6.justification: Table 5 newly reports CellFlux/CellFluxRL score pairs of 0.45/0.52 for MoA-CLIP, 0.34/0.40 for MoA-DINO, and 0.88/0.95 for NuInCy-StarDist. These corroborate the existing improvement trend; previously reported numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, reward formulas, optimization objectives, and algorithmic derivations remain unchanged. Appendix F introduces empirical evaluation without new formal assumptions, propositions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: biological reward design, RL post-training, and additional gains through test-time scaling. The new evaluation supplies supporting evidence without redefining these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix F newly interprets agreement across independent evaluators as evidence against exploiting reward-specific implementation details. Reward hacking was already discussed in v1, but this cross-evaluator interpretation is new; the existing limitations discussion is retained.

D1.justification: v4 newly identifies the original MoA classifier as Inceptionv3 and specifies CLIP, DINOv2, and StarDist for the additional evaluation. Existing implementation and compute disclosures remain unchanged, while detailed training settings for the new classifiers are not supplied.

R1.justification: v4 adds references for DINOv2, CLIP, and StarDist to support Appendix F. The related-work discussion and positioning relative to CellFlux, DiffusionNFT, and other generative approaches remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 adds Appendix F, removes the duplicated abstract heading, updates equal-contribution and equal-advising annotations, and extends the acknowledgment. The main prose and existing section organization are largely unchanged.

P2.justification: v4 adds Table 5 and makes limited changes to abstract width, caption formatting, table spacing, and pagination. Figures 1–8 retain their visual content, and existing tables are preserved.

improvement.justification: v1's quantitative biological validation primarily reused the optimized reward evaluators. Appendix F and Table 5 provide useful independent corroboration through CLIP, DINOv2, and StarDist, strengthening evidence against evaluator-specific reward hacking. The improvement is bounded because the new evaluator training and evaluation settings remain sparsely documented and the results lack uncertainty estimates.
